questions.question: What is scalability in system design?
options: The ability to add more features to a system
The ability of a system to handle increased load by adding resources
The ability to reduce system complexity
The ability to write better code
questions.explanation: Scalability is the ability of a system to handle increased load by adding resources to the system while maintaining performance.

questions.question: What is vertical scaling?
options: Adding more machines to your pool of resources
Adding more power (CPU, RAM) to your existing machine
Creating backup copies of your system
questions.explanation: Vertical scaling (scale up) means adding more power to your existing machine, such as upgrading CPU, RAM, or storage.

questions.question: What is horizontal scaling?
options: Adding more machines to your pool of resources
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out) means adding more machines to your pool of resources, distributing the load across multiple servers.

questions.question: Which scaling approach typically has higher complexity but nearly unlimited capacity?
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling has higher complexity due to distributed system challenges but offers nearly unlimited capacity since you can keep adding more machines.
